root_cause.text: The xe_pagefault_service function was missing validation to reject write and atomic access attempts to read-only VMAs, allowing unauthorized memory modifications through the page fault handler.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a critical check immediately after VMA lookup in xe_pagefault_service that was previously absent. The new code block checks `if (xe_vma_read_only(vma) && pf->consumer.access_type != XE_PAGEFAULT_ACCESS_TYPE_READ)` and returns `-EPERM` to deny the operation. The absence of this validation in the original code (referenced by the Fixes tag pointing to commit fb544b844508) meant that write and atomic page faults could proceed on read-only VMAs without being rejected, violating memory protection semantics.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add permission check to reject write/atomic access attempts on read-only virtual memory areas during pagefault handling.
intent_record.what: Added a new conditional guard block that checks if a VMA (virtual memory area) is read-only and the pagefault access type is not a read operation. If both conditions are true, the function sets err to -EPERM and jumps to the unlock_vm label.
intent_record.how: This change prevents write or atomic access operations on read-only VMAs by returning a permission error (-EPERM) before proceeding with pagefault handling. It enforces memory protection semantics by rejecting non-read access attempts on read-only memory regions.
